description: Updates an existing QuantConnect project with new code or configuration settings. It takes the project ID and the updated content as inputs to synchronize changes on the cloud platform.

name: mcp__quantconnect__backtest_strategy
description: Initiates a backtest for a specified trading strategy within the QuantConnect environment. It accepts parameters such as the project ID, start date, end date, and cash balance to execute the simulation and return results.

name: mcp__quantconnect__deploy_live_trading
description: Deploys a verified strategy to production for live trading on the QuantConnect platform. It requires the project ID and target brokerage account details to activate the algorithm in real-world market conditions.

name: mcp__ramparts__scan_yara_rules
description: Executes provided YARA rules against a specified set of files or directories to detect patterns matching the rule definitions. Main inputs include the YAML/compiled YARA rule definition and the target file paths.

name: mcp__ramparts__perform_static_analysis
description: Runs static analysis on source code files to identify potential security vulnerabilities, such as hardcoded secrets or unsafe function calls, without executing the code. Main inputs include the source code content or file path and optional configuration parameters for sensitivity.

name: mcp__ramparts__validate_mcp_server_config
description: Checks the MCP server's configuration files for common security misconfigurations, such as exposed endpoints or insecure transport settings. Main inputs include the configuration file content or path.

name: mcp__ramparts__get_yara_rule_library
description: Retrieves a list of available or built-in YARA rules that can be used for scanning, optionally filtered by category or keyword. Main inputs include an optional search query string to filter the rule set.

name: mcp__ramparts__get_static_analysis_report
description: Retrieves the detailed results of a previous static analysis run, including severity levels and locations of detected issues. Main inputs include the unique identifier or timestamp of the specific analysis session.

name: mcp__ramparts__update_yara_rules
description: Updates the local YARA rule database by fetching the latest versions from a specified remote source or updating custom rules. Main inputs include the URL of the rule repository or the path to a local directory containing updated rule files.

name: mcp__ros2__list_nodes
description: Retrieves a list of all active ROS2 nodes in the current system namespace. It takes an optional 'namespace' parameter to filter results by specific ROS2 namespace.

name: mcp__ros2__get_node_info
description: Fetches detailed metadata for a specific ROS2 node, including its state, uptime, and connected topics/services. The main input is the 'node_name' string.

name: mcp__ros2__list_topics
description: Lists all currently available ROS2 topics with their associated message types and publisher/subscription counts. It accepts an optional 'topic_type' filter to narrow down results.

name: mcp__ros2__echo_topic_message
description: Subscribes to a specific topic and captures the most recent message payload for inspection. The inputs include 'topic_name' and optionally 'num_messages' to limit the output count.

name: mcp__ros2__list_services
description: Returns a list of all registered ROS2 services along with their request/response type definitions. It takes an optional 'service_type' parameter to filter by specific interface types.

name: mcp__ros2__send_service_request
description: Sends a synchronous request to a specified ROS2 service and returns the response payload. The inputs are 'service_name' and 'request_data' formatted as a JSON-serializable dictionary matching the service's request type.

name: mcp__schogini-mcp-image-border__add_border_to_image
description: Applies a specified border style and color to an input image. It requires the base64-encoded source image, border width, and border color as inputs.

name: mcp__schogini-mcp-image-border__get_base64_output
description: Returns the final processed image with the added border encoded in base64 format. It takes the path or ID of the image processing job as its main input to retrieve the result.

name: mcp__schogini-mcp-image-border__validate_image_input
description: Checks if the provided base64 string is a valid image and determines its current dimensions. It accepts the raw base64 string and optional format constraints as inputs.

name: mcp__short-io__create_short_link
description: Creates a new shortened URL using Short.io's link shortener service. It accepts parameters such as the original destination URL, custom alias, and optional title or expiration date.

name: mcp__short-io__get_link_analytics
description: Retrieves performance metrics and click data for a specific shortened link or domain. It requires the short code or full URL as input to fetch statistics like total clicks, geographic location of visitors, and referral sources.

name: mcp__short-io__list_domains
description: Returns a list of all domains configured and active in the Short.io account. This tool helps identify which custom domains are available for use when creating new short links or analyzing domain-specific performance.

name: mcp__stackgen__deploy_application
description: Deploys a specified application to the target cloud infrastructure, accepting parameters for the application name, environment (e.g., staging or production), and deployment configuration details.

name: mcp__stackgen__monitor_system_health
description: Retrieves current health metrics and status reports for monitored resources, requiring an optional scope filter such as a specific service, region, or instance ID to narrow the results.

name: mcp__stackgen__list_infrastructure_resources
description: Returns a comprehensive inventory of existing cloud infrastructure assets, allowing users to specify resource types (like EC2 instances, S3 buckets, or RDS databases) and filtering criteria.

name: mcp__stackgen__configure_networking_rules
description: Updates firewall rules, security groups, or VPC configurations for the managed cloud environment, requiring inputs such as rule direction, protocol, port range, and CIDR blocks.

name: mcp__telnyx__send_message
description: Sends a text message to a specified phone number using the Twilio-compatible Telnyx messaging API. Main inputs include the destination 'to' number, the source 'from' phone number, and the message body content.

name: mcp__telnyx__make_call
description: Initiates a voice call to a target phone number using Telnyx telephony services, allowing for real-time audio communication or integration with IVR systems. Main inputs include the destination 'to' number, the source 'from' number, and optional connection instructions like an answer webhook URL.

name: mcp__telnyx__get_phone_numbers
description: Retrieves a list of available phone numbers associated with the user's Telnyx account that can be used for messaging or calling. Main inputs include optional filters such as country code, phone number type (e.g., local, toll-free), and capability requirements.

name: mcp__vuln-nist-mcp-server__search_cves_by_id
description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific CVE identifier from the NVD API. The primary input is the 'cve_id' parameter, which should be a string like 'CVE-2023-1234'. It returns formatted text results suitable for LLM consumption.

name: mcp__vuln-nist-mcp-server__search_cves_by_query
description: Searches the NVD/CVE database using keywords, product names, or vendor information within a specified date range. It accepts inputs such as 'keyword', 'vendor', and 'start_date'/'end_date', utilizing automatic query chunking for large ranges.

name: mcp__vuln-nist-mcp-server__get_cve_details
description: Fetches comprehensive metadata and descriptions for one or more specific CVE IDs. The main input is a list of 'cve_ids'. It optimizes performance by processing multiple IDs in parallel via the MCP protocol.

name: mcp__vuln-nist-mcp-server__search_vulnerabilities_by_date_range
description: Executes a broad search for vulnerabilities updated or published within a specific time window, handling large date ranges through automatic chunking. Inputs include 'start_date' and 'end_date', returning aggregated formatted results to improve performance via parallel processing.

name: mcp__waystation__notion_search_pages
description: Searches for pages or databases within a Notion workspace based on specified query parameters. Main inputs include the search query string, optional filter criteria (such as date ranges or specific property values), and pagination limits.

name: mcp__waystation__slack_send_message
description: Sends a text message to a designated Slack channel or direct message thread. Main inputs are the target channel ID or user ID, the message content string, and optional configuration for timestamped replies or threaded responses.

name: mcp__waystation__asana_create_task
description: Creates a new task within a specified Asana project or portfolio. Main inputs include the target project ID, the task name, optional description text, assigned user IDs, and due date information.

name: mcp__waystation__monday_com_create_item
description: Adds a new item (row) to a specific board in Monday.com with defined column values. Main inputs are the board ID, the item name, and a dictionary of column IDs mapped to their respective value types (e.g., status, date, person).

name: mcp__waystation__fetch_integrations_list
description: Retrieves a list of currently available third-party business tool integrations supported by the server. Main inputs are minimal, typically requiring no parameters or optional filters to categorize results by tool type (e.g., CRM, communication, project management).

name: go-module-management.md
description: When the project structure lacks a `go.mod` file or uses Go modules inconsistently, Claude must initialize the module with the correct project path and ensure all dependencies are explicitly listed in the go.mod file rather than relying on indirect references.

name: error-handling-conventions.md
description: When writing functions that may fail, Claude must wrap errors using `fmt.Errorf` with `%w` for wrapping or `errors.New` for simple static strings, and never return raw interface{} types without explicit typing.

name: context-propagation.md
description: When defining functions that perform I/O operations or long-running tasks, Claude must accept a `context.Context` as the first parameter and use it to control cancellation and timeout behavior for all underlying calls.

name: struct-field-naming.md
description: When defining new data structures, Claude must export fields only when necessary for JSON marshaling or external package access by using explicit JSON struct tags, keeping internal logic fields unexported.

name: interface-segregation.md
description: When designing abstractions, Claude must define small, specific interfaces close to the consumer rather than large general interfaces, ensuring that implementers only provide methods they actually need.

name: test-file-organization.md
description: When generating test code, Claude must place table-driven tests in files named `_test.go` adjacent to the source file and use `t.Run` for subtests to ensure granular failure reporting.

name: dependency-injection-pattern.md
description: When creating service constructors, Claude must accept dependencies via explicit interface types in the constructor arguments rather than instantiating implementations directly within the function body.

name: goroutine-safety-guards.md
description: When sharing data between goroutines, Claude must strictly enforce mutual exclusion using `sync.Mutex` or `sync.RWMutex` for mutable state, and avoid relying on channel-only patterns for complex shared memory scenarios.

name: logging-structure.md
description: When adding logging statements, Claude must use a structured logger like `slog` or `zap` with named fields rather than simple string formatting to enable better traceability and filtering in production environments.

name: main-package-entry.md
description: When generating the entry point for a service, Claude must keep the `main` package minimal by delegating initialization logic to an internal `cmd` or `app` package that handles configuration loading and server startup.

name: rust-crate-metadata-structure.md
description: When creating or modifying a Rust crate's root files, ensure that `Cargo.toml` explicitly declares all dependencies with their features and the `[package]` section adheres to SemVer guidelines. Define clear `categories` and `keywords` to improve discoverability, and always include a `README.md` at the project root.

name: rust-dependency-versions.md
description: When specifying dependencies in `Cargo.toml`, avoid using wildcard versions (e.g., `*`) and instead pin to specific minor versions or use caret requirements (`^1.0.0`) to allow for safe updates. Always check `crates.io` for the latest stable version before adding a new dependency.

name: rust-feature-flag-strategy.md
description: When designing a library, use Cargo features to enable optional functionality and keep the core crate lightweight by default. Document every available feature in the `README.md` and ensure that no two features create conflicting behavior without explicit documentation.

name: rust-doc-comment-standards.md
description: Write Rustdoc comments for all public APIs, including functions, structs, enums, and traits. Include at least one usage example in the doc comment using the ```rust syntax block and ensure that panic conditions are documented with `# Panics` or `# Errors` sections.

name: rust-derive-macro-conventions.md
description: When defining structs or enums, explicitly derive common traits like `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, and `Serialize/Deserialize` (if using Serde) unless there is a clear performance or semantic reason to omit them. Ensure that all derived fields support the requested trait.

name: rust-error-handling-patterns.md
description: Define custom error types for your crate and implement `std::error::Error` for them instead of returning boxed errors or simple strings. Use the `thiserror` crate to simplify error type definitions and ensure that all public functions return `Result<T, E>` with a documented error variant.

name: rust-test-coverage-requirements.md
description: Ensure that every public function has at least one integration test and one unit test covering happy path and edge cases. Use the `#[cfg(test)]` attribute to isolate test code and maintain a high level of branch coverage for critical logic paths.

name: rust-lint-configuration.md
description: Configure `clippy.toml` or `[lints]` sections in `Cargo.toml` to suppress false positives but enable all warnings by default. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` and fix all lint errors before committing changes.

name: rust-version-stability-policy.md
description: Set the minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) in `Cargo.toml` and document it clearly in the repository. Do not use unstable features or nightly-only APIs unless explicitly marked as such in the crate's configuration.

name: rust-changelog-management.md
description: Maintain a `CHANGELOG.md` file that follows the Keep a Changelog format and update it with every release candidate. Group changes by 'Added', 'Changed', 'Deprecated', 'Removed', 'Fixed', and 'Security' categories.

name: incidents-require-log-analysis-first.md
description: When an incident is reported or a critical error occurs, Claude must immediately analyze relevant log files before suggesting any fixes or code changes. Do not propose solutions until the root cause has been identified through log inspection.

name: incidents-avoid-breaking-changes.md
description: During active incident response, Claude must strictly avoid suggesting breaking API changes, database schema alterations, or major architectural refactors. Focus only on immediate stabilization patches and configuration adjustments that preserve system integrity.

name: incidents-prioritize-rollback-over-fix.md
description: If a recent deployment is suspected to be the cause of an incident, Claude must prioritize suggesting a rollback strategy before attempting to write new corrective code. Provide clear instructions for reverting to the last known good state.

name: incidents-require-impact-assessment.md
description: Before providing any solution, Claude must explicitly assess the potential impact of the proposed fix on other services and users. Warn clearly if a suggested action might widen the outage or affect unaffected parts of the system.

name: incidents-use-safe-defaults.md
description: When suggesting configuration changes to mitigate an incident, Claude must default to conservative values that favor system stability over performance. Explicitly state why a safe default is being chosen over a more aggressive optimization.

name: incidents-verify-rollout-strategy.md
description: If the solution involves deploying a new patch, Claude must ensure the proposed rollout strategy includes a canary or phased release mechanism. Never suggest a simultaneous full-production deployment for an untested incident fix.

name: incidents-document-rationale.md
description: For every action taken during incident response, Claude must include a concise comment or documentation explaining the 'why' behind the decision. This ensures that post-mortem reviews can clearly understand the context of emergency changes.

name: incidents-validate-monitoring-alerts.md
description: After suggesting a fix, Claude must verify that appropriate monitoring alerts and dashboards are updated to detect recurrence or side effects. Ensure that observability tooling reflects the new state of the system being patched.

name: incidents-segment-communication.md
description: When drafting communication or status updates for an incident, Claude must keep technical jargon minimal and focus on business impact and ETA. Structure the message to clearly separate current symptoms from root cause findings for non-technical stakeholders.

name: incidents-schedule-post-mortem.md
description: Upon resolution of an incident, Claude must automatically generate a structured template for a blameless post-mortem report. Include sections for timeline reconstruction, root cause analysis, and specific action items to prevent recurrence.

name: spring-boot-architecture.md
description: applies_when: The codebase involves Spring Boot application structure or file organization. directive: Organize all Java packages by feature domain rather than by technical layer to ensure high cohesion. Place controllers, services, repositories, and DTOs within their respective feature directories instead of grouping them globally.

name: dependency-injection-principles.md
description: applies_when: Writing or refactoring Spring beans, constructors, or service injections. directive: Prefer constructor injection over field injection using @Autowired to ensure immutability and testability. Explicitly define all dependencies in the public constructor and mark the class as final where appropriate.

name: spring-data-jpa-best-practices.md
description: applies_when: Implementing repository interfaces or writing database queries. directive: Derive queries from method names or use @Query with named parameters instead of string concatenation to prevent SQL injection. Avoid the N+1 problem by using EntityGraphs or JOIN FETCH in your JPQL/HQL queries.

name: exception-handling-strategy.md
description: applies_when: Managing errors, validations, or REST API responses. directive: Use @ControllerAdvice for global exception handling to standardize error response formats across the application. Create specific custom exceptions for business logic failures rather than returning raw stack traces to clients.

name: spring-security-config.md
description: applies_when: Configuring security filters, JWT tokens, or role-based access control. directive: Extend WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter or implement the new SecurityFilterChain bean approach for modern Spring Security versions. Never hardcode credentials; use Spring Vault or environment variables for sensitive configuration.

name: spring-boot-testing-standards.md
description: applies_when: Writing unit tests, integration tests, or mock server configurations. directive: Use @SpringBootTest with WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT for full context integration tests and Mockito for pure unit tests. Always reset mocks and verify interactions to ensure test isolation and prevent side effects.

name: spring-boot-properties-configuration.md
description: applies_when: Reading configuration files, application.yml, or environment variables. directive: Use @ConfigurationProperties with a prefix for type-safe binding instead of @Value annotations for multiple properties. Provide default values in the POJO fields to handle missing configuration gracefully during local development.

name: spring-boot-rest-api-standards.md
description: applies_when: Defining REST controllers, endpoints, or HTTP status codes. directive: Adhere strictly to HTTP methods and status codes (e.g., 201 Created for POST, 404 Not Found for missing resources). Return ResponseEntity objects explicitly to control headers and status codes rather than relying on implicit Spring defaults.

name: spring-boot-logging-conventions.md
description: applies_when: Adding log statements or configuring log levels. directive: Use the SLF4J API with parameterized logging (e.g., logger.info("User {} logged in", userId)) to avoid string concatenation overhead. Ensure that sensitive data like passwords or tokens are never written to logs.

name: spring-boot-docker-integration.md
description: applies_when: Creating Dockerfiles, docker-compose files, or CI/CD pipelines for Spring apps. directive: Use multi-stage builds to minimize the final image size by separating the Maven/Gradle build stage from the JRE runtime stage. Include health checks in the Dockerfile that point to a dedicated actuator endpoint for reliable orchestration.
